metadata.title: 5 Things to Know Before the Stock Market Opens on Thursday

content.text:
Stock futures are lower amid a tech sector sell-off this morning; Alphabet shares plunged after a disappointing earnings report from the Google parent; Microsoft shares rose after the company's results topped Wall Street estimates; Amazon is set to follow with its own third-quarter report tonight; and shares of Marvell and Lumentum are making big moves after a report that the companies are in deal talks. Here's what you need to know today.
Nasdaq Futures Sink as Tech Stocks Slide
Stock futures are lower Thursday as the AI trade stumbles following earnings reports from Alphabet and Microsoft (more on that below). Nasdaq futures were down 1.1% recently, while futures linked to the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.3%. The major indexes each posted a gain of less than 0.3% yesterday, rising for a third straight session, after the Federal Reserve left its key interest rate unchanged, as expected. WTI crude oil futures were down 1% at $101.90 per barrel, while gold futures ticked lower to $4,040 an ounce, and bitcoin traded around $80,100, down from yesterday's high of $81,700. The yield on the 10-year Treasury was holding steady around 5.02%.
Alphabet Stock Plunges After Disappointing Results
Alphabet (GOOGL) shares were down more than 10% before the opening bell and on track to hit their lowest point since early April, after the Google parent missed expectations with its third-quarter results. The company late Wednesday reported earnings per share of $2.12 on revenue of $127.58 billion. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha had called for EPS of $2.94 on revenue of $127.89 billion. While cloud revenues roughly doubled to $30.7 billion, ahead of projections, search and advertising revenues fell short. The results could add fuel to worries about Google's ability to generate enough revenue from its new AI products to provide a return on its massive investments in data centers and AI hardware. Coming into today's session, Alphabet shares had gained 4% since the start of the year, lagging the S&P 500's 13% gain over the period.
Microsoft Stock Rises on Solid Earnings
Microsoft (MSFT) shares were gaining ground in premarket trading, after the tech giant posted fiscal first-quarter results that topped analysts' estimates on the top and bottom lines. The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $4.89 on revenue that grew 19% year-over-year to $92.28 billion, above expectations, as cloud sales surged. For the first time in an earnings release, Microsoft broke out revenues from its Azure cloud, which rose 48% to $33.17 billion. Broader cloud revenues jumped 30% to $63.9 billion. Microsoft has faced similar questions to Alphabet and others in the AI trade about whether they are overspending to get ahead in the AI race, but Microsoft's latest report could ease some of those fears for now. Microsoft shares, which have gained roughly 10% in 2026, were up 1.5% in recent premarket trading.
